outcome: Success rate of IUBT for severe postpartum haemorrhage (PPH)
Factors predicting IUBT failure (defined as need for arterial embolisation or surgery)
cohort: Women treated with IUBT for severe PPH from July 2010 to March 2013 in ten maternity units in a perinatal network (N = 226)
finding: Intrauterine balloon tamponade is an effective method for treating severe PPH, and early deployment before the development of coagulopathy increases its success rate.
mod_finding: IUBT success rate was significantly higher after vaginal delivery (88.9%) than caesarean delivery (65.5%, P < 0.01); caesarean delivery was a predictor of IUBT failure.
